record.paper_title: Open questions on prominences from coordinated observations by IRIS, Hinode, SDO/AIA, THEMIS, and the Meudon/MSDP
record.original_question: For the oblique prominence threads seen in the large arches observed in 304 Å, is the rapidly moving cool material produced by fast cooling of EUV-emitting plasma, or are the observed opposite flows better explained by longitudinal oscillations that generate counter-streaming, or by large-scale siphon flows between regions of different magnetic strength?

evidence.quote: These oblique threads may be found along the field lines in the large arches observed in 304 Å. Is it fast moving cool material due to fast cooling of EUV plasma? There is counter streaming along these features.

counter streaming could occur because of longitudinal oscillations (Chen et al. 2014; Luna et al. 2014). The material in the dips could travel on one side or the other side. For large scale structures the siphon flow mechanism could be more important than the counter streaming leading to large flows towards one end of the prominence or the other end.

artifact.status_search_result: The question concerns an unresolved problem in solar physics about the origin of fast flows along oblique prominence threads. Recent literature on prominence dynamics (e.g., reviews by Luna, Karpen, Antolin and others on thermal non-equilibrium condensations, longitudinal oscillations, and counter-streaming) continues to debate the relative importance of condensation, oscillation-driven counter-streaming, and siphon flows; no single mechanism has been definitively established as the cause for large-arch oblique threads. The question therefore appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Review of prominence oscillations (Arregui, Oliver, Ballester)
status_evidence.snippet: Longitudinal oscillations and counter-streaming flows in prominence threads remain actively investigated, with multiple competing models.
status_evidence.claim: The mechanisms producing counter-streaming and longitudinal flows in prominence threads are still under debate.

status_evidence.title: Luna et al., Large-amplitude longitudinal oscillations in solar prominences
status_evidence.snippet: Studies show longitudinal oscillations can produce apparent counter-streaming, but condensation and siphon flows also remain plausible explanations for observed flows.
status_evidence.claim: No consensus has been reached on whether oscillations, condensation, or siphon flows dominate fast oblique thread motions.
